written: 2026-10-22 ~08:50 JST, before any v14 episode; requested by the round-2 reviewer of the paper draft (docs/paper/reviews/review_full_round2.md), run under the user's instruction that missing data be produced on CloudPC-2
kind: frozen controllers, no training; analysis + four cheap experiments

d1.what: paired delta of each v11 SNN centre relative to the classical + ES centre (seed 1) on the v11 nominal blind set and on every v12/v13 scenario; 0 new episodes
d1.reading: parity with the same-budget classical if the CI covers 0

d2.what: the opponent with its base-law pulses not suppressed during schedule segments, on the v11 nominal set, the primary kick set and the x1.5 turbulence set (576 episodes)
d2.reading: if this arm crashes about as rarely as the SNN under the hit, the SNN advantage is "pulses on vs off", not closed loop; if it crashes like the opponent, the deficit is the open-loop schedule

d3.what: channel ablation of the five frozen v11 centres under the primary hit: pulses suppressed while in charge (nopulse), set-points zeroed while in charge (noref); 1920 episodes
d3.reading: if nopulse crashes like the opponent and noref like the full centre, the robustness travels with the pulse channel

d4.what: the imitation starts of seeds 2-5 under the primary hit and the x1.5 turbulence (1536 episodes)
d4.reading: is the robustness of the imitation start a property of one seed or of the architecture

d5.what: replication of the primary 3 mN m mid-manoeuvre hit on a fresh base 2_102_500_000 with the 14 arms (blind12 test kick_rep)
d5.reading: does H1 (>= 3 of 5 v11 seeds) replicate

expectations: d2: the un-suppressed opponent will fire a few extra pulses but still crash often (the schedule is still open loop); d3: nopulse will lose most of the advantage, noref less; d4: the other imitation starts will be about as robust as seed 1; d5: H1 replicates (4-5 of 5) given the 2 and 4.5 mN m levels
